topic.title: Filters vs a chat
topic.claim: Our parents' generation made matchmaking worse by adding filters, while the oldest elders just talk to people.
topic.behaviour: Families screen candidates through long checklists on matrimony sites, forward very few profiles, and reject people for small filters before anyone has actually met.
topic.mechanism: Parents carry the fear of living with the consequences, so they filter hard to avoid regret. A grandparent chatting casually collects the kind of information no profile shows.
topic.group: Indians in their late 20s and parents of marriageable children
real_details: A poster said a cousin searched for a year, and his parents forwarded exactly two profiles, both mismatches
The 90-year-old grandfather dropped most of the filters and chatted with the girl's parents
He found a match in two months that the cousin and his parents accepted
Commenters argued whether elders really have a skill or whether it's one lucky sample
One commenter said parents are cautious because they must live with the outcome, grandparents less so
topic.why_now: The thread is a top post this month and divided commenters on whether the old way worked.

score.reason: Fresh generational contrast on matchmaking filters, broad mirror for anyone near rishta conversations
score.best_hook: Our grandparents found a match over one evening of tea and gossip. Our parents need four meetings and a spreadsheet. We call that progress.
